Airports: availability, accuracy and limitations

For the 100 busiest European airports and the 100 busiest airports worldwide: how often OPDI has each main item, how close it is to the records, and where it is limited.

Search an airport, or an item, to see how often OPDI has each main item there, how close it is to the records, and what limits it. The figures are those of the three days measured; the references are explained on Data quality.

How to read a card

Each item has two labels, kept apart: availability (high, partial, low) and accuracy (good, fair, limited, too few compared, no reference), each with the count it is computed over. The rules are in How to read the labels. Departure items are counted among the departures, arrival items among the arrivals.

Outside Europe most items show availability only (see Per item); a low share means the item is mostly missing, a high one only that it exists. An item found there may still be wrong.

Look up an airport or an item

The search below needs JavaScript. Every figure is also in the files under Every other item.

Which airports

  • European list: the 100 European airports with the most departures and arrivals in the Network Manager records. Of them, 72 send airport records; at the other 28, take-off and landing times are compared with Network Manager, and block times, runways and stands have no reference.
  • Worldwide list: the 100 airports with the most departures and arrivals in OPDI’s own flight list. Of them, 70 are outside Europe and 30 in Europe, 28 of which send airport records. The ranking favours the regions where OpenSky has many receivers.

An airport in both lists appears once, with both ranks and its European figures.

Per item

Type an item’s name in the search, or click one of the item chips, to see every airport grouped by its label. Under “All airports” and “Worldwide top 100”, the airports where the item has no reference are grouped apart, by availability. Outside Europe the departure and destination airports are compared with Network Manager, but only for the flights to and from Europe (see What OPDI is compared with); the other items have no reference there.

Patterns

The patterns and the three lists below cover the European airports only.

Take-off and landing times are good at most airports. Block times and stands are the weak items: at most airports they are low in availability, and where they can be compared, the off-block time is mostly labelled limited (it is often later than the record), the in-block time more often fair. Departure and destination airports are good almost everywhere.

Where an item is unreliable

At these airports an item was compared with the records at least 30 times and fewer than half of OPDI’s values agree with them. Do not use the item there without checking it.

Three cases stand out:

  • At Bergen (ENBR), Stavanger (ENZV) and Trondheim (ENVA), the runway OPDI names never agrees with the record, while the take-off and landing times there mostly do. This suggests that the runways are named differently in OPDI’s runway table and in the records, rather than that the aircraft used other runways; it has not been checked. Do not use rwy_dep, rwy_arr or info.runway at these airports.
  • At Malta (LMML), most take-off times and most runways disagree with the records, while the landing times mostly agree. Do not use the take-off times or the runways there.
  • At İstanbul Airport (LTFM), OPDI has a take-off time for almost no departure and a landing time for fewer than half of the arrivals. Positions near Istanbul are often disturbed (spoofed), which is possibly the cause.

Where ground events are nearly absent

At these 38 airports, fewer than 2 % of OPDI’s departures have an off-block time and fewer than 2 % of its arrivals an in-block time: the receivers near the airport hear almost no aircraft on the ground. Block times, stands and the airport surface events are then missing, not wrong. Take-off and landing times can still exist, because they need reception only near the runway in the air. The table covers the European list; the warning on an airport’s card applies to every airport.

Where no take-off or landing time exists

At these 10 airports OPDI has no take-off time and no landing time on any of the three days, although its flight list has flights there. At most of them OPDI also gives the airport as destination for only a small share of the recorded arrivals. The cause has not been established; do not use these airports for runway or arrival studies.
